03 · Episode Text

Check what you missed.

Read the notes after listening. Check what you missed.

Have you finished the listening questions?

Episode notes

Neil and Pippa look back at what social media used to be: MySpace, Facebook, Twitter — places to message friends and post photographs. In less than a generation the internet changed, and the rise of AI changed it again. A pair of BBC World Service presenters describe an AI-generated photograph so strange that they cannot say what it is meant to be, which is the point: it is now hard to tell what a human made and what a machine made.

A recent report found that social media activity reached its peak in 2022 and has been going down ever since. The writer Kyle Chayka dates his own turning point earlier, to 2015–16, when Twitter became the centre of American election argument. Until then the internet had felt like somewhere you went to enjoy yourself; the political anger ended that for him.

Looking forward, Chayka expects the large platforms and the tech giants to keep pushing AI-generated content, and expects users not to want it. He treats it as a novelty rather than a permanent change, and expects people to drift away from the big platforms towards smaller spaces and closer contact with individual voices — posting less overall.

The quiz answer: the first electronic message, sent in 1844 by dots and dashes tapped on a telegraph wire, was Morse code.

04 · Language Bank

Useful language for change over time.

Direction

peakTrend

Reach the highest point.

TRzirveye çıkmak · en yüksek noktasına ulaşmak

Use withactivity / sales / interest / membership peaked in 2022 · reach a peak in … · peak at + figure

Social media activity peaked in 2022 and has been falling ever since.

declineFormal word

Become lower or smaller; a fall or reduction.

TRgerilemek · düşüşe geçmek · gerileme

Use witha decline in + the thing (a decline in users) · a decline of + the size (a decline of 12%)

decline steadily / sharply / gradually

The decline in daily posting has been steady rather than sudden.

Tip More formal than going down; useful in academic and data-focused writing.

drift away fromMovement

Gradually become less interested in, involved with, or connected to something — often without one clear moment when it happened.

TRyavaş yavaş uzaklaşmak · kopmak

Use withdrift away from a platform / a habit / a group · people are drifting away

Users are drifting away from the biggest platforms rather than deleting their accounts.

gravitate towardsMovement

Be naturally drawn to something.

TRkendiliğinden yönelmek · çekim duymak

Use withgravitate towards smaller spaces / familiar voices / people like themselves

Readers gravitate towards writers whose voice they recognise.

Timeframe

ever sincePattern

From then until now.

TRo günden bu yana

Use witha past event + present perfect ever since

a past event + present perfect continuous ever since

Activity peaked in 2022 and has been falling ever since.

Tip Needs an earlier time point in the sentence or context

for nowTime phrase

True now.

TRşimdilik

Use withend of the sentence, most often · for now, at least · at least for now

AI images are a novelty, for now.

Tip Limits the statement to the present

in less than a generationTime phrase

Within the span of one generation.

TRbir kuşak dolmadan

Use within less than a generation, X has changed / grown / fallen

In less than a generation, social media has changed how news reaches people.

Prediction

may continue toPattern

Say that something may keep happening.

TR… devam edebilir

Use withX may continue to grow / fall / rise · could continue to

The large platforms may continue to push AI-generated content.

Tip may = possible · is likely to = probable · will = more direct

may see + object + -ing formPattern

Describe a change you expect to see.

TR… olduğunu görebiliriz

Use withwe may see more users leaving

We may see more people moving to smaller platforms.

NOTE

After perception verbs such as see, hear, watch, notice, feel and observe, we can use either the bare infinitive or the -ing form. The meaning is slightly different:

  • I saw her dance. — I saw the whole event, from beginning to end.
  • I saw her dancing. — I saw the action while it was happening.
noveltyWord

Something interesting because it is new or unusual.

TRyenilik · yeni olduğu için ilgi çeken şey

Use witha novelty · the novelty wears off · novelty value

He treats AI-generated content as a novelty rather than a permanent change.

Tip In “a novelty for now”, for now suggests it may not last

More useful language

Learn these too. Use them when they fit.

behemothExtra

An extremely large, powerful company.

Common in journalism and commentary. It emphasises very large size or power.

lean intoExtra

Commit to something rather than resist it.

Common in business and media writing.

hubExtra

The centre where something gathers.

Twitter became the hub of election argument. Also: a transport hub.

Say this — not that

Too broad → more precise

Make the time clear. Add a period, a current trend, or a cautious prediction.

social media is dead

social media activity has fallen since 2022

soon nobody will use the big apps

many users are drifting away from the largest platforms

AI content will disappear

AI content may prove to be a novelty

people will move to smaller platforms

we may see more people moving to smaller platforms

it went down a lot

it declined sharply between 2022 and 2024

06 · Sentence Lab

Build five sentences.

Read the example. Then write your own sentence.

1Peak and change

Say when something peaked and what happened next.

Example

Newspaper circulation reached its peak in the late 1980s and has been declining ever since.

Your sentence

______ peaked in ______ and has ______ ever since.

Use a date or figure you know. Otherwise choose another example.

2Gradual movement

Describe a gradual move away from something.

Example

Younger viewers are drifting away from scheduled television.

Your sentence

______ are drifting away from ______.

Use a different expression for a sudden change.

3Cause

Give the cause.

Example

Constant advertising turned many users away from the platform.

Your sentence

______ turned many ______ away from ______.

Give a specific cause.

4Prediction

Make a cautious prediction.

Example

We may see more students choosing shorter courses over the next few years.

Your sentence

We may see + object + -ing form + time phrase.

Replace may with will. Compare the level of certainty.

5Your own sentence

Write one sentence about how your own social media use has changed. Use one Bank item and a clear timeframe.

Example

I have been posting less since the start of last year, though I could not say why.

Your sentence

Write one sentence.

Quick check

  • Is each time reference clear?
  • Are your predictions cautious where needed?
  • Did you include a timeframe where it helps?
